title: Atlas Freight: late shipment AT-5521
transcript:
Agent: Atlas Freight support, this is Leo. How can I help?
Customer: Hi Leo, this is Sam from Atlas Freight. We have a shipment that is three days late. The tracking page has not updated since Friday.
Agent: I am sorry about that. Can you give me the shipment number?
Customer: AT-5521. It is a full truckload from Columbus to Kansas City. The customer is threatening a chargeback.
Agent: I see the shipment. It left Columbus on September 11 and was last scanned at the Indianapolis hub on September 12. There is no departure scan from Indianapolis.
Customer: So it is sitting there?
Agent: It looks that way. I am opening a carrier trace now. The carrier has 24 hours to respond with a location and an updated delivery estimate.
Customer: Can you also notify the customer? They are asking for a new ETA.
Agent: Yes. I will send an update with the trace number and tell them we are treating it as priority. I cannot promise a new ETA until the carrier responds.
Customer: What if it does not move by tomorrow?
Agent: If there is no update by tomorrow afternoon, I will escalate to the carrier's regional manager and look at a recovery option. I will schedule a follow-up for September 17.
Customer: Please make sure someone calls me, not just an email.
Agent: I have scheduled a phone follow-up for September 17. I will also add your direct number to the ticket.
Customer: Thanks, Leo. This is a big account for us.
Agent: I understand. I will keep the ticket at high priority.
